A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet of Things is still a very immature and insecure space, with many of the devices not having the basic security features we expect from our laptops and mobile devices.
we present a security analysis of smart locks, which are commodity Internet of Things devices.

the security of smart locks can be improved by: (1) ensuring that the lock's firmware is not easily compromised, (2) preventing the lock from being remotely controlled by unauthorized users, (3) preventing unauthorized users from learning information about the lock owner, (4) preventing the lock owner from being tracked through the lock, (5) ensuring that the physical security of the lock is not compromised, and (6) ensuring that the user's intended actions are communicated to the lock.
The main takeaway from our work is that
security must be a primary concern when designing IoT devices.
the security of commodity IoT devices must be considered early in the design phase and not just in the context of the device's primary function.
the security of commodity IoT devices must be addressed in their design and development, rather than being an afterthought or a patchwork of fixes applied to existing products.
